highlights.content: [![AIM](/assets/aim-logo-0ZnRqAR3.png)](/) [Subscribe](/subscribe) Article Complete [![AIM](/assets/aim-logo-0ZnRqAR3.png)](/) Google Launches Two New TPUs for Enterprise Agentic AI Workloads ![Google Launches Two New TPUs for Enterprise Agentic AI Workloads](/cdn-cgi/image/width=1600,quality=60,format=auto,fit=scale-down/https://zdpdvwhvukelzzbzbjvh.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/imported-images/1768653174699-f74c2acc-6af7-4221-b186-c1f3401ed8ef-g6uysc.webp) [AI News](/ai-news) # Google Launches Two New TPUs for Enterprise Agentic AI Workloads TPU 8tx is built for confidential AI inference, allowing enterprises and governments to process sensitive data. [Siddharth Jindal](/author/siddharth-jindal) Published Updated ## Key takeaways * Google has launched TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, expanding its TPU portfolio for enterprise AI workloads. * TPU 8tx focuses on confidential AI inference, enabling secure processing of sensitive data for enterprises and governments. * TPU 8i Max is designed for large context windows and multi-agent workloads, addressing the need for advanced AI reasoning capabilities. * The TPU 8tx system incorporates hardware-level security to protect data during processing, ensuring confidentiality. * Both new systems aim to enhance performance, with TPU 8tx offering lower latency compared to its predecessor. 5 min Follow[Preferred Source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://analyticsindiamag.com)[Google News](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqMggKIixDQklTR3dnTWFoY0tGV0Z1WVd4NWRHbGpjMmx1WkdsaGJXRm5MbU52YlNnQVAB?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)[WhatsApp](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VaCAfcMGehEGsj0COi2R)[Telegram](https://t.me/joinchat/TrPapX0NesB579PQ) [Google](https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/sarvam-ai-appoints-ex-google-cloud-india-md-sashikumar-sreedharan-as-president-and-cbo) has expanded its eighth-generation [Tensor Processing Unit (TPU)](https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news/openai-plans-to-purchase-google-tpus-report) portfolio with two new systems, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, to meet the computing requirements of enterprises deploying autonomous AI agents. The two systems target different workloads. TPU 8tx is built for confidential AI inference, allowing enterprises and governments to process sensitive data while models are running. TPU 8i Max, meanwhile, is designed to handle large context windows and workloads involving multiple AI agents. “With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models’ massive context windows,” Google said in a blog post. The expanded portfolio also includes TPU 8t, built for large-scale model training, and TPU 8i, designed for low-latency reasoning. TPU 8tx is optimised for secure and confidential inference, particularly for regulated enterprises and government organisations running proprietary AI models and autonomous agents. The system uses the same silicon as TPU 8t and is paired with fifth-generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts. Google has built security into the hardware layer to protect data and model weights even while they are being processed. Typically, data is encrypted when stored or transferred over a network but must be decrypted when processed in memory. TPU 8tx is designed to address this gap through hardware-level confidential computing. Google said the system can deliver up to 2x lower latency compared with TPU 8t, with a near-zero performance penalty. It also allows organisations to fine-tune models using private datasets, distil larger models into smaller ones, and train AI agents through reinforcement learning without moving sensitive data between separate computing clusters. The second system, TPU 8i Max, addresses memory bandwidth constraints that emerge when multiple AI agents work across large software codebases or process hours of video. highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Self-Hosted LLM vs API: $0.70 to $2.00 Input [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 10, 2026 · 28 min read Moonshot’s own [Kimi K3.1 Pro pricing page](https://www.kimi.ai/resources/kimi-k3-1-pro-pricing) lists $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens, while Mistral Large 4 sits at $0.70 and $2.10 on Mistral’s price list. Those two numbers frame the decision every team faces in November 2026: pay a hosted API by the token, or download the weights and run a self-hosted LLM on your own metal. Four open-weight families dominate that choice right now. Kimi K3.1 Pro from Moonshot AI, GLM-5.3 from Z.ai, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and Mistral Large 4 (nicknamed “Le Chonk”) all shipped or updated inside the last three months, and all claim frontier-class coding. A straight [ranking of open-source LLMs](https://shattered.io/best-open-source-llm-october-2026-kimi-glm-deepseek/) tells you which one scores highest. It does not tell you which one you can afford to run, and that is where most self-hosting projects stall. Three numbers decide the outcome. Total parameters set how much memory you must buy. Active parameters set how fast each token comes out. Your monthly token volume sets whether a fixed cluster bill beats a metered one. highlights.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # SK Telecom, Rebellions, NVIDIA partner for Korea AI infrastructure South Korean firms SK Telecom and Rebellions are collaborating with NVIDIA to advance the country's AI infrastructure. This partnership integrates data centers, processors, and an open infrastructure platform to enhance sovereign AI capabilities. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 05:10 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google") Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google ## Highlights * SK Telecom, Rebellions, and NVIDIA are collaborating on South Korea’s AI infrastructure. * Rebellions will integrate its Rebel R200 NPUs with NVIDIA’s platform via NVLink Fusion. * SK Telecom plans to deploy these integrated systems, drawing on its data center expertise. * South Korea’s government supports this initiative with significant funding for sovereign AI. South Korean telecommunications firm [SK Telecom](/tag/sk+telecom), AI chip startup [Rebellions](/tag/rebellions), and [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) have announced a collaboration to advance [South Korea](/tag/south+korea)’s [AI infrastructure](/tag/ai+infrastructure). This initiative aims to integrate [data centers](/tag/data+centers), processors, and an open infrastructure platform. Rebellions will use [NVLink Fusion](/tag/nvlink+fusion) to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to NVIDIA’s infrastructure platform. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, leveraging its data center expertise, according to a press release from NVIDIA. Jung Jai-hun, SK Telecom Chief Executive Officer and President, stated this collaboration validates the potential of next-generation [sovereign AI](/tag/sovereign+ai) infrastructure. He added it combines global AI infrastructure technology with Korean AI semiconductors. Sunghyun Park, Rebellions co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, noted that Korean technology would lead in powering AI worldwide. Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and Chief Executive Officer, highlighted Korea's talent and ambition to be a world leader in AI. The firms plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference. This will assign different stages of AI response generation to the best-suited processor architecture. The plan includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput. ### Government Support and Investment South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) supports this collaboration to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI infrastructure. Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, said this enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA. The government will actively support this collaboration, he added, to deliver tangible results and advance cooperation with NVIDIA. Earlier this month, the South Korean government allocated KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) in its budget for 2027. This funding supports the development of physical AI, data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model. The government also plans to train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

AI Summary Anthropic unveiled its large language models Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, designed to strengthen scientific research and coding. The company said Fable 5.2 is aimed at general users and blocks most biology research questions and many cybersecurity requests, while Mythos 5.2 relaxes limits for verified researchers. Anthropic reported benchmark gains in science and coding, improvements in safety filtering, faster response modes, and token prices 20 percent lower than the prior generation. * Writer Seung-a Yoo (유승아) * published 2026-11-11 09:26:23 * updated 2026-11-11 09:28:03 Link copied to clipboard. ![](https://cdn.digitaltoday.co.kr/news/photo/202611/714445_661793_518.jpg) Anthropic unveiled Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 with enhanced performance for scientific research and coding. [Photo: Shutterstock] Anthropic unveiled the large language models (LLMs) “Claude Fable 5.2” and “Claude Mythos 5.2,” which it said strengthen scientific research and coding performance. On Nov. 10 (local time), IT outlet SiliconANGLE reported that the two models are Anthropic’s best-performing models to date. They share the same core capabilities, but differ in the level of safeguards in biology and cybersecurity. Fable 5.2 is offered to general users and blocks most biology research questions and many cybersecurity-related requests. Mythos 5.2, by contrast, is a version with relaxed restrictions and is available only to verified researchers through two restricted-access programs. The scale of the performance improvement was confirmed in benchmarks. Anthropic compared Fable 5.2 with the prior model across 14 AI evaluations and said it scored more than 10 percent higher than Fable 5.1 in most categories. In Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which assesses scientific research capabilities, it scored 74.6 percent, an improvement of 22 percent from the prior model. It also delivered results in complex mathematics research. Anthropic said it took 11 days for a previously undisclosed model to convert a well-known mathematical theorem into a form that can be verified by computer, but Fable 5.2 cut the time to 30 hours by parallelising calculations using 1,000 agents. In separate research, it presented answers to two unsolved problems in theoretical physics related to black holes. Mythos 5.2 also demonstrated performance in life sciences. It analysed 34 capsids, the protective shells of the harmless AAV virus, and accurately modelled the structures of 28 of them. AAV capsids are used to deliver drugs in some treatments. This is meaningful in that it analysed a complex structure composed of dozens of proteins. Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold2, used in biology research, is a model that predicts individual protein structures. Coding performance also improved sharply. Fable 5.2 posted performance more than 13 percent higher than the previous model on two coding benchmarks, FrontierCode 2.0 and FrontierSWE v2. In an experiment in which Anthropic engineers assigned it to build an operating system, more than 1,000 agents wrote and verified code for about 8 days to complete a functioning operating system. The operating system runs on a laptop and supports network connections and Claude functions. Safety and efficiency were also improved. When Fable 5.2 receives restricted biology or cybersecurity requests, it routes them to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Anthropic said the likelihood of incorrectly blocking safe requests fell 55 percent versus the prior model. Anthropic presented the two models as suitable for complex and open-ended technical tasks. highlights.content: # Meituan releases open weights for its trillion-parameter LongCat multimodal model under the MIT license ![Meituan releases open weights for its trillion-parameter LongCat multimodal model under the MIT license](/media/news_images/meituan-releases-open-weights-for-its-trillion-parameter-longcat-multimodal-mode.jpg) Meituan, the Chinese food delivery and e-commerce group, published the weights of LongCat-2.5 on Hugging Face under the MIT license on Nov. 9, about a week after introducing the model [[2]](https://venturebeat.com/technology/meituan-releases-the-open-weights-of-its-longcat-2-5-llm-with-vision-under-a-permissive-mit-license). The MIT license allows commercial use, modification and redistribution; Meituan's license does not grant rights to its trademarks or patents [[1]](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.5)[[2]](https://venturebeat.com/technology/meituan-releases-the-open-weights-of-its-longcat-2-5-llm-with-vision-under-a-permissive-mit-license). LongCat-2.5 is a mixture-of-experts model built on LongCat-2.0, with 1.6 trillion total parameters and about 48 billion activated per token, according to the model card [[1]](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.5). (The Hugging Face metadata lists 1.8 trillion, a discrepancy VentureBeat also flagged [[2]](https://venturebeat.com/technology/meituan-releases-the-open-weights-of-its-longcat-2-5-llm-with-vision-under-a-permissive-mit-license).) It handles text, images and video, converting visual features into discrete tokens processed alongside text, and has switchable thinking and non-thinking modes [[1]](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.5). ## Meituan's benchmark claims All scores below come from Meituan's model card. On the harder Terminal Bench v4.0 it still trails Claude Opus 5 by more than 15 points [[1]](https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.5). VentureBeat cautioned that public leaderboard results use different setups and are not a clean head-to-head [[2]](https://venturebeat.com/technology/meituan-releases-the-open-weights-of-its-longcat-2-5-llm-with-vision-under-a-permissive-mit-license). The collaboration will see Rebellions’ next-generation R200 neural processing units ([NPUs](https://www.eenewseurope.com/en/tags/npu)) integrated into NVIDIA’s MGX rack architecture, with deployment planned at SK Telecom’s AI data centers. The agreement highlights growing opportunities for custom AI accelerators to work alongside NVIDIA GPUs in large-scale inference systems. For European semiconductor developers and data center operators, it offers a potential blueprint for combining domestic AI silicon with established computing infrastructure to support sovereign AI initiatives. ## NVLink Fusion connects custom AI silicon Rebellions plans to use NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to connect its R200 NPUs through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, targeting energy-efficient inference for frontier AI models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architectures. The NVIDIA MGX rack architecture will provide standardized system designs, while its ecosystem of original design manufacturers and component suppliers could help Rebellions accelerate development and reduce deployment complexity. “Today’s announcement marks a turning point, opening a new chapter for sovereign AI by connecting Korea’s AI silicon and models with global systems technology,” said Sunghyun Park, cofounder and CEO of Rebellions. The companies also plan to explore disaggregated inference, splitting AI workloads between different processor architectures. Under the proposed approach, NVIDIA GPUs would handle the compute-intensive prefill stage, while Rebellions NPUs would manage token generation during decoding. This division of labor is intended to improve inference throughput and power efficiency, potentially addressing two major challenges facing AI data center operators. ## SK Telecom targets full-stack sovereign AI SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems within its AI data center infrastructure, connecting the hardware with proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, and public-facing AI services. The initiative supports Korea’s government-backed “AI for All” project and aims to strengthen domestic control over AI infrastructure, models and services. Standardizing rack footprints, power delivery and cooling through NVIDIA MGX could also simplify integration of GPU and NPU systems within existing data center environments. ## Government backing and 2028 deployment Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT is supporting the collaboration as part of a broader effort to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI capabilities and domestic semiconductor industry. [Chinese](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/china/) [embodied AI](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/embodied-ai/) company [Robbyant](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/robbyant/) has released an open-source [AI model](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/ai-model/) designed to give robots a better sense of touch and improve their ability to handle objects. Called LingBot-Touch, the model converts signals from different tactile sensors into a common format that robotic control systems can use. [According to the company](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261109284905/en/Robbyant-Releases-LingBot-Touch-to-Bring-General-Purpose-Touch-Perception-to-Robots), which is part of the [Ant Group](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/ant-group/), trained it on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data and evaluated it in 26 tests involving two robotic hands and four AI action models. In one test, a Sharpa Wave robotic hand controlled by the T-Rex model successfully unscrewed a bottle cap 56.25% of the time without tactile feedback. Feeding raw sensor signals directly into the action model increased the success rate to 62.5%, while LingBot-Touch raised it to 90%, according to Robbyant. ### Combining Different Types of Touch Sensors Robotic hands use different sensing technologies to detect contact and pressure, but their signals can vary depending on the sensors and how they are arranged. highlights.content: ## w.media Audios Listen to latest: The rack, not the room South Korean telecommunications firm SK Telecom, AI chip startup Rebellions, and NVIDIA have announced a collaboration that aims to advance South Korea’s AI infrastructure by bringing together data centers, processors, and an open infrastructure platform. As outlined by NVIDIA in a press release, Rebellions will use NVLink Fusion to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to NVIDIA’s infrastructure platform. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, drawing on its expertise in the data center space. “This collaboration is meaningful in that it validates the potential of next-generation sovereign AI infrastructure by combining global AI infrastructure technology with Korean AI semiconductors,” said Jung Jai-hun, SK Telecom Chief Executive Officer and President. “As a leading Korean AI silicon startup, we will lead the charge to establish Korean technology as a core pillar powering AI worldwide,” said Sunghyun Park, Rebellions co-founder and Chief Executive Officer. “Korea has the talent, technology and industrial ambition to become a world leader in AI,” said Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and Chief Executive Officer. “Sovereign AI gives nations the power to turn their language, culture and expertise into intelligence.” Together, the firms plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference. This will assign different stages of AI response generation to the processor architecture best suited to the task at hand. The plan includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput. The collaboration is supported by South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), which sees it as a means to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI infrastructure. “This collaboration with NVIDIA marks a significant step forward, as it enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA, a global leader in AI computing, through NVLink Fusion,” said Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT. “The government will actively support this collaboration to deliver tangible results and further advance cooperation with NVIDIA across a range of areas, including physical AI and securing GPU supply.” Earlier this month, w.media reported that the South Korean government had set aside KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) in its budget for 2027 to support the development of physical AI, data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model. The South Korean government will also train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. Listen to latest: The rack, not the room

AI Agents.content: UPDATED 19:18 EST / NOVEMBER 10 2026 ### AMD introduces Epyc 6 processors for AI agent workloads Advanced Micro Devices Inc. today debuted a new line of central processing units for servers. The Epyc 6 series, which is also known as Venice, comprises 10 CPUs that are organized into two groups. The first set includes chips with a large number of relatively slow cores. The remaining CPUs feature fewer, higher-frequency cores. Both chip collections feature optimizations designed to speed up artificial intelligence agents. AI agents run their neural networks on graphics cards and use CPUs to power their tools, the applications with which they carry out work. CPUs also perform certain other tasks in machine learning clusters. According to AMD, Epyc 6 chips can support up to 3.3 more agents per watt than Nvidia Corp.’s Vera CPU. The company says that its processor series also outperforms comparable Intel Corp. silicon. Deploying an AI agent’s tools on CPUs with a relatively small core count can reduce software expenses in some cases. Certain enterprise applications, notably databases, are billed according to the number of cores on which they run. As a result, deploying a database on one high-frequency core is cheaper than using two slower ones that together provide the same amount of processing power. The two highest frequency Epyc 6 chips have a base speed of 4.05 GHz. They can boost their clock to 5.3 GHz when running demanding workloads. Both chips have 96 cores and a 384-megabyte cache. The two densest Epyc 6 chips, meanwhile, include 256 cores with a base speed of 2.55 GHz. Each core can power two threads, or stream of calculations, for a total of 512 threads. That enables the chips to run a large number of AI agents at once. Some large language models spin up hundreds of agents or more when tackling complex tasks. The Epyc 6 series is based on a new core architecture called Zen 6. Its IPC, a key measure of CPU performance, is 31% higher than AMD’s previous design when running AI workloads. The increase partly stems from the fact that AMD uses Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s latest two-nanometer node to make Zen 6 cores. The cores come in two editions. There’s a version simply called Zen 6 that is optimized for clock speed and a scaled-down edition, Zen 6c, for CPUs with high core counts. The latter core includes an enhanced out-of-order processing mechanism not available in the standard edition. The mechanism performs some calculations well before the results are needed to save time. Zen 6 also includes AI-specific optimizations. The architecture is compatible with the FP16 data format, which makes it possible to compress the information processed by agents to lower their hardware usage. There’s also improved support for VNNI-INT8, a technology that condenses multiple AI calculations into a single operation to save time. “AI is significantly expanding the role of the CPU across every layer of the data center,” said Dan McNamara, the senior vice president and general manager of AMD’s Compute and Enterprise AI unit. “With 6th Gen AMD EPYC, customers can standardize on the proven x86 foundation while choosing a workload-optimized solution to run more agents,” AMD says that a number of major data center suppliers have already started shipping servers equipped with Epyc 6 chips. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 10:49 EST / NOVEMBER 10 2026 ### The next chapter for Red Hat: AI agents rewrite the cloud-native playbook by A.J. Bram Red Hat LLC has spent years making Kubernetes manageable for enterprises that would rather run applications than tend clusters. As AI agents move into production, the company is extending that experience to a new generation of workloads. AI agents don’t just consume infrastructure. Red Hat arrives at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City this week with a growing portfolio of technologies addressing those requirements. OpenShift provides the Kubernetes foundation; its work with Nvidia Corp. on OpenShell addresses agent execution and security; and the llm-d project has reached version 1.0 with capabilities for serving the context-heavy workloads agents create. Together, these developments position Red Hat to help enterprises manage agentic AI through open, Kubernetes-based infrastructure. Unlike conventional applications, autonomous agents can generate commands, invoke tools and delegate work across multiple systems. That flexibility creates opportunities for automation while increasing the importance of consistent access controls and oversight. This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of how cloud-native infrastructure is evolving to support enterprise AI, with Red Hat and the broader Kubernetes ecosystem addressing the security, operational efficiency and scalability requirements of autonomous agents. (\* Disclosure below.) ### Red Hat advances Kubernetes-native security for AI agents The rapid adoption of OpenClaw has brought renewed attention to agent security. An agent that can read files, run shell commands and make network calls needs clearly defined permissions and isolation to operate safely within enterprise environments. Red Hat’s response centers on its collaboration with Nvidia around OpenShell, a runtime that places agents inside isolated execution environments and applies policy to their access. Nvidia developed OpenShell; Red Hat is working with Nvidia and the wider community to integrate the technology into Red Hat AI and its open hybrid cloud platform. Red Hat’s announcement describes the work as part of a broader effort to bring security-focused agentic AI capabilities to enterprise infrastructure. OpenShell uses sandboxing, process-aware policy and controls over network access and credentials. Red Hat has also described how OpenShell can work with OpenShift’s sandboxed containers, adding application-level restrictions inside a virtual-machine boundary. These complementary layers govern agent behavior and isolate the environments in which agents operate, as Red Hat explains in its technical overview of layered sandboxing. The distinction matters because sandboxing does not make an agent trustworthy. It limits the damage an agent can cause when its instructions, generated code or external inputs lead it somewhere they should not. AI Agents.titleZh: Trent AI builds multi-agent code-to-doc system on OpenClaw, TechGig
AI Agents.content: [![techmonk logo](/_icons/logos/techmonk-logo-mobile-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI](/news/ai) * 2 minRead # Trent AI builds multi-agent code-to-doc system on OpenClaw Trent AI has developed a multi-agent system using OpenClaw to automate public documentation generation from code. This pipeline aims to address documentation drift in fast-paced engineering environments. * [TechGig](/agency/87450652/TechGig "TechGig") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 06:45 AM IST ## Highlights * Trent AI built a multi-agent code-to-doc pipeline on OpenClaw for automated documentation. * The system uses Change Scanner, Doc Classifier, Doc Publisher, and Orchestrator agents. * Deployment on AWS prioritised security with no public IP and restricted egress. * GitHub App permissions and branch protection limit agent actions and require human review. Trent AI has built a multi-agent system on [OpenClaw](/tag/openclaw) to automate the generation of public documentation from code, the company said. This initiative aims to address documentation drift, where engineering teams ship features rapidly while documentation falls out of date. The system uses OpenClaw's agentic capabilities and is composed of several agents. These include a Change Scanner, a Doc Classifier, a Doc Publisher, and an Orchestrator, along with [GitHub](/tag/github) Tools. ### Multi-agent system architecture The Change Scanner reads code repositories, fetches merged pull requests, and identifies impacted files. The Doc Classifier triages changes into categories like breaking changes or new features, assigning a confidence score. The Doc Publisher converts raw files into customer-facing documents, reconciles existing documentation, and creates a pull request with updated content. An Orchestrator coordinates these components, tracks failures, and runs the pipeline on a schedule. GitHub Tools are scripts connecting to GitHub, used by the Change Scanner and Doc Publisher. Trent AI developed an agent for each component to understand [multi-agent systems](/tag/multi-agent+systems). OpenClaw currently lacks clear context handoff for multi-agent work, so Trent AI used shared files for context exchange. This is a common practice for long-running agents. ### Secure AWS deployment Trent AI deployed the agents safely on AWS, guided by principles of least privilege and a tight blast radius. The system only receives necessary access, and any compromise remains contained within the documentation pipeline. A security review, using Trent's Claude Code Security, identified threats such as data exfiltration, code pollution, and secret leakage. Mitigations were mapped to risks for each agent and network path. The AWS deployment uses a single EC2 instance within a VPC, without a public IP or inbound rules. Access is limited to AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, removing the need for SSH keys. Egress traffic is controlled by AWS Network Firewall with a stateful FQDN allow-list. This restricts the instance to communicating only with essential services like GitHub and the Bedrock control plane. Agents authenticate via a dedicated GitHub App installed only on the relevant repository, with permissions scoped to pull\_requests:read+write and contents:read+write. No admin access or metadata writes are permitted. GitHub's branch protection requires human review for every pull request opened by the agents. The agents can propose changes but cannot merge their own work. OpenClaw's agentToAgent setting, a boolean with an allow-list of agent IDs, gates inter-agent calls. This limits the blast radius of [prompt injection](/tag/prompt+injection) attacks to the documentation pipeline agents. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

AI Agents.titleZh: TI redefines embedded development with agentic AI in its CCStudio™ ecosystem, empowering engineers to accelerate innovation — TradingView News
AI Agents.content: ![]() ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-light.svg) ![PR Newswire](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/pr_newswire--theme-dark.svg) # TI redefines embedded development with agentic AI in its CCStudio™ ecosystem, empowering engineers to accelerate innovation ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/texas-instruments.svg) Agentic AI integration at every stage of embedded development dramatically shortens time to market, including a purpose-built skill that reduces software migration time from months to days **News highlights:** DALLAS, Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Texas Instruments (TI) (Nasdaq: TXN) today announced significant enhancements to its CCStudio™ ecosystem, strengthening its agentic artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities in order to streamline embedded software development across microcontroller (MCU), wireless connectivity and radar applications. Moving beyond generative code assistance toward autonomous development, the CCStudio ecosystem's agentic AI framework injects device-specific knowledge directly into the AI tools engineers already use, enabling them to accelerate complex design tasks from months to days and focus on system-level design and innovation. TI is showcasing these innovations at electronica 2026, Nov. 10-13, in Munich, Germany. For more information, see [ti.com/CCStudio](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4816782-1&h=2375476702&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ti.com%2Fdesign-development%2Fccstudio-development-ecosystem.html%3Fhqs%3Depd-tech-data-agenticai_null-pr-pp-null-ww_en&a=ti.com%2FCCStudio). "Embedded software development is an incredibly manual and time-consuming process that has been significantly changing over the last few years with agentic AI," said Amichai Ron, senior vice president, Embedded Processing and DLP® Products at TI. "TI was one of the first semiconductor companies to enable agentic AI workflows in our development ecosystem, and over the last several months, we have been strengthening its capabilities to enable significantly better productivity. Device migration, system configuration and debugging are all integrated with agentic AI built on TI's embedded expertise. Our goal is to give developers a more efficient and accurate development experience so they can spend more time innovating." **A new era of embedded development**For the last two years, generative AI tools have been helping engineers write code faster. However, they often struggle to complete complex embedded development tasks given the lack of hardware-specific context. TI's CCStudio development ecosystem has been augmented with an agentic AI framework to address this challenge. Through context engineering, the framework injects device-specific knowledge, including software development kits (SDKs), pin configurations and peripheral data, directly into the workflow through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Grounding AI models in TI data improves accuracy, reduces hallucinations and produces implementation-ready outputs. The architecture retrieves and delivers only the most relevant technical context to the model, reducing latency and token costs. For example, TI's CCStudio integrated development environment (IDE) exposes its core capabilities to industry-standard AI agents, allowing them to generate code, configure peripherals, build the application, flash it to the device and debug it autonomously. Engineers can use simple language to move through the full development workflow in CCStudio IDE or CCStudio for VS Code, all without switching tools or rebuilding context. A straight [ranking of open-source LLMs](https://shattered.io/best-open-source-llm-october-2026-kimi-glm-deepseek/) tells you which one scores highest. [Photo: Shutterstock] Anthropic unveiled the large language models (LLMs) “Claude Fable 5.2” and “Claude Mythos 5.2,” which it said strengthen scientific research and coding performance. On Nov. 10 (local time), IT outlet SiliconANGLE reported that the two models are Anthropic’s best-performing models to date. They share the same core capabilities, but differ in the level of safeguards in biology and cybersecurity. Fable 5.2 is offered to general users and blocks most biology research questions and many cybersecurity-related requests. Mythos 5.2, by contrast, is a version with relaxed restrictions and is available only to verified researchers through two restricted-access programs. The scale of the performance improvement was confirmed in benchmarks. Anthropic compared Fable 5.2 with the prior model across 14 AI evaluations and said it scored more than 10 percent higher than Fable 5.1 in most categories. In Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which assesses scientific research capabilities, it scored 74.6 percent, an improvement of 22 percent from the prior model. It also delivered results in complex mathematics research. Anthropic said it took 11 days for a previously undisclosed model to convert a well-known mathematical theorem into a form that can be verified by computer, but Fable 5.2 cut the time to 30 hours by parallelising calculations using 1,000 agents. In separate research, it presented answers to two unsolved problems in theoretical physics related to black holes. Mythos 5.2 also demonstrated performance in life sciences. It analysed 34 capsids, the protective shells of the harmless AAV virus, and accurately modelled the structures of 28 of them. AAV capsids are used to deliver drugs in some treatments. This is meaningful in that it analysed a complex structure composed of dozens of proteins. Google DeepMind’s AlphaFold2, used in biology research, is a model that predicts individual protein structures. Coding performance also improved sharply. Fable 5.2 posted performance more than 13 percent higher than the previous model on two coding benchmarks, FrontierCode 2.0 and FrontierSWE v2. In an experiment in which Anthropic engineers assigned it to build an operating system, more than 1,000 agents wrote and verified code for about 8 days to complete a functioning operating system. The operating system runs on a laptop and supports network connections and Claude functions. Safety and efficiency were also improved. When Fable 5.2 receives restricted biology or cybersecurity requests, it routes them to Opus 4.8 or Opus 5. Anthropic said the likelihood of incorrectly blocking safe requests fell 55 percent versus the prior model. Anthropic presented the two models as suitable for complex and open-ended technical tasks. LLMs.titleZh: Large Language Models Struggle to Convert Infrastructure Condition Data
LLMs.content: ![BIOENGINEER.ORG](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/logo_sariyazi.png) ![Bioengineer.org](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/logo352-e1516556386659.png) # Large Language Models Struggle to Convert Infrastructure Condition Data into Knowledge Graphs ![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=80&r=g) ![Large Language Models Struggle to Convert Infrastructure Condition Data into Knowledge Graphs](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/stackrss-featured-3587-750x422.png) Large Language Models Struggle to Convert Infrastructure Condition Data into Knowledge Graphs A comparative evaluation of leading commercial and open-source artificial intelligence systems has revealed that large language models are not yet dependable enough to autonomously convert transportation infrastructure condition data into standardized semantic knowledge graphs. In an investigation conducted by engineering researchers Lea Höltgen, Sven Zentgraf, Philipp Hagedorn, and Markus König, published in AI in Civil Engineering, four advanced models—OpenAI’s gpt-4o and gpt-4-turbo, alongside Meta’s open-source llama-3-70b-instruct and llama-3.1-405b-instruct—were benchmarked on their capacity to translate relational database records of bridge inspections into formal Resource Description Framework statements using the W3C RDB to RDF Mapping Language standard. The experimental findings demonstrated that while models can reliably craft basic structured queries and adhere to template structures, their persistent misapprehension of complex mapping mechanics, relational joins, and domain ontologies produces erratic errors that preclude unassisted real-world deployment in the architecture, engineering, and construction sector. Relational databases have long served as the digital cornerstone of structured information management across infrastructure agencies, ensuring tabular data integrity, record consistency, and storage efficiency through strict relational schemas and constraints. Within the construction industry, historical records are often segregated across isolated stakeholder silos, proprietary software tools, or obsolete legacy formats. Transforming these disparate records into interconnected knowledge graphs structured via the Resource Description Framework provides a flexible environment where data entities and their interrelationships are explicitly defined as subject-predicate-object triples. This formal semantic enrichment facilitates automated cross-domain reasoning, location-based analyses, and advanced querying via SPARQL that surpasses standard SQL capabilities, yet established manual transformation protocols like R2RML remain notoriously labor-intensive, demanding rare dual expertise in database administration and formal ontologies. To rigorously determine whether modern natural language processors can automate this translation hurdle, the research team developed a four-stage sequential pipeline designed to isolate and assess intermediate transformation stages. The experimental workflow began with SQL query generation, where models converted natural language prompts into executable database queries against a provided schema. The second phase, SQL-to-ontology mapping, directed the language models to align extracted database tables and attributes with corresponding conceptual classes and properties defined in standardized construction vocabularies, outputting structured JSON schemas. In the third phase, the models generated comprehensive R2RML mapping documents in Turtle syntax based on the established ontology alignments. In the terminal phase, specialized external mapping engines, namely the Morph-KGC processor and the RDFLib framework, executed the generated mapping rules against the relational database to synthesize final RDF triples. This staged architecture deliberately allowed the research framework to validate intermediate outputs, execute programmatic self-correction routines upon detecting syntax failure...

AI Product.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Anthropic Ships 4 Office Tools to Rival Microsoft [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Nov 10, 2026 · 14 min read Anthropic stepped into Microsoft’s home turf on November 10, 2026. At an event in San Francisco, the company unveiled four workplace products named Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data, and [Engadget framed the push as Anthropic taking on both Google and Microsoft](https://www.engadget.com/2312177/anthropic-takes-on-google-and-microsoft-with-claude-sheets/). The new Anthropic office tools turn Claude from a chat window into something closer to a teammate that sits in meetings, edits spreadsheets and builds dashboards. Anthropic summed up the pitch in one line: “Starting today, Claude can build spreadsheets, whiteboards, and dashboards with your team.” The sentence matters because it moves Claude out of the personal-assistant lane and into shared work, where the money in enterprise software has always sat. The timing also draws attention. Reports describe an anticipated Anthropic public offering, and the launch landed while investors were already sizing up the company. Our earlier analysis of [what Amazon and Google could gain from an Anthropic IPO](https://shattered.io/amazon-google-411-billion-anthropic-ipo-windfall-2026/) covers the investor side. This piece stays on the products, the competitive stakes and what is still unproven. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## What Anthropic Announced on November 10 Anthropic PBC announced four products in one event. Claude Meetings is an AI assistant that joins video calls. Claude Sheets is a spreadsheet tool. Claude Whiteboards is a brainstorming canvas. Claude Data, which Anthropic previously called Claude Dashboards, connects Claude to company systems and produces dashboards. Bloomberg’s headline put the strategic angle in plain terms, and [Bloomberg Law’s republished version of the story](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/anthropic-unveils-office-tools-ahead-of-ipo-taking-on-microsoft) says Anthropic unveiled office tools ahead of its IPO, taking on Microsoft. Fortune ran a similar story under a headline about a new suite of AI office productivity tools in the run-up to the IPO. Both outlets tie the launch to the offering. Neither framing proves that the offering has closed, and as of today it has not. Availability splits by product. Claude Data is generally available to all paid plans. Claude Sheets and Claude Whiteboards are in beta for paid plans. Claude Meetings is in beta for Team and Enterprise subscriptions only. [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/servicenow.svg)NOW](/symbols/NYSE-NOW/) shares are falling Tuesday as enterprise software stocks slide after Anthropic launched Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data, products that may reignite fears of AI pressure on software companies. Here’s [what you should know](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63080302/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-futures-rise-nasdaq-100-futures-fall-as-trump-signals-iran-war-to-end-fairly-soon-crwv-ttwo-bw-in-focus). ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/servicenow.svg) **ServiceNow Stock Falls as Anthropic Expands Claude** Programmers have already changed how they work thanks to Claude Code, and Anthropic now wants other teams to benefit too. The Claude maker said its assistant can now draft sheets, boards and dashboards alongside coworkers. The aim, Anthropic wrote, is to “bring that magic to every team.” With Claude Sheets, people and the assistant share a spreadsheet, editing formulas on several tabs. Claude Whiteboards gives meeting attendees a digital canvas and lets Claude summarize their conclusions afterward. Narrated short videos, data visuals and dashboards come out of Claude Data, which was called Dashboards before and pulls from tools such as Snowflake and Salesforce. A fourth feature, Claude Meetings, will join calls to jot down notes and arrives soon. The launch may revive “SaaSpocalypse” worries, a shorthand for fears that AI tools will undercut established software companies and that have weighed on the industry recently. Partners such as Adobe and Atlassian can now run their apps inside Claude, thanks to upgraded interactive connectors. Sales reps, accountants and HR staff get ready-made skills from new plugins by Salesforce, NetSuite and Workday, with Salesforce and Workday still in beta. Anthropic’s marketplace lists over 9,000 connectors, along with plugins. Large customers receive administrative tools. Managers pick the products and connectors staff may use and can cap spending. Security teams can inspect activity through records of use, plus a compliance interface that connects to 100-plus tools, such as Splunk and CrowdStrike. **ServiceNow Launches Continuous Control Monitoring** On the same day, ServiceNow rolled out always-on control monitoring driven by AI agents inside its Integrated Risk Management product. Over 100 packaged connections let it watch systems outside ServiceNow, including cloud, container, identity, software and on-site tools. The agents handle three jobs: they create the checks, explain what the test results mean and take action once a control breaks. The system can also open tickets or fix problems on its own within set policies. ServiceNow’s Vasant Balasubramanian said the aim is “making assurance a live signal across the enterprise.” **NOW Shares Are Slipping** **NOW Price Action:** [ServiceNow shares](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NOW) were down 4.75% at $97.88 at the time of publication on Tuesday, according to [Benzinga Pro](https://www.benzinga.com/pro/register-3). **Disclaimer** *Preview Image: JarTee/Shutterstock* *Preview Image: JarTee/Shutterstock* ## Compare charts ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from Benzinga](/news-flow/?provider=benzinga) Select market data provided by [ICE Data Services](https://www.ice.com/fixed-income-data-services). AI Product.titleZh: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks | TechCrunch
AI Product.content: Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets. The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks. With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai. The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says. Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins. Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow. As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines. The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time. When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says. Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile. The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet. Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did. Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile. Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos. Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace. [Chinese](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/china/) [embodied AI](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/embodied-ai/) company [Robbyant](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/robbyant/) has released an open-source [AI model](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/ai-model/) designed to give robots a better sense of touch and improve their ability to handle objects. Called LingBot-Touch, the model converts signals from different tactile sensors into a common format that robotic control systems can use. [According to the company](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261109284905/en/Robbyant-Releases-LingBot-Touch-to-Bring-General-Purpose-Touch-Perception-to-Robots), which is part of the [Ant Group](https://theaiinsider.tech/tag/ant-group/), trained it on nearly 5,000 hours of real-world tactile data and evaluated it in 26 tests involving two robotic hands and four AI action models. In one test, a Sharpa Wave robotic hand controlled by the T-Rex model successfully unscrewed a bottle cap 56.25% of the time without tactile feedback. Feeding raw sensor signals directly into the action model increased the success rate to 62.5%, while LingBot-Touch raised it to 90%, according to Robbyant. ### Combining Different Types of Touch Sensors Robotic hands use different sensing technologies to detect contact and pressure, but their signals can vary depending on the sensors and how they are arranged. As a result, a model trained to interpret one type of sensor may not work with another, requiring developers to collect additional data and retrain their systems. Robbyant claims LingBot-Touch addresses the problem by processing signals from different sensors through separate encoding pathways and mapping contact points into a shared fingertip coordinate system. While previous approaches involved devising detection methods by defining patterns for phone numbers, address books, and resident registration numbers in code to classify types, this model is characterized by its ability to detect sensitive information and anomalies by analyzing context through self-learning based on a Large Language Model (LLM)." Kim Sam-young, CTO of QueryPay, stated as much during an interview with Money Today on the 10th, saying, "Various methods have been utilized, ranging from regular expressions and keyword rules to statistical and machine learning classification. However, QEV overcomes the limitations of existing methods that identified sensitive information only within the scope of pre-defined or learned types." The company explained that QEV is the first domestic product in the category of AI decision models. It is a model specialized for security in the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) field, which prevents the leakage of corporate sensitive information. The company has moved to secure technological leadership by reflecting recent corporate demand regarding data breaches. According to CTO Kim, QEV analyzes input sentences to classify information and determines its own optimization. Unlike general generative AI, which focuses on answering questions or creating new content, QEV judges whether given information meets specific conditions and presents an appropriate result among predefined options along with the probability for each option. CTO Kim said, "QEV can determine whether a sentence contains personal information or internal corporate secrets if an employee inputs customer data or undisclosed business materials into an AI service." He added, "It will be possible to identify situations before sensitive information leaks externally and to conduct reviews and responses in accordance with security policies." QEV implements proprietary decision-making AI technology based on the open-source AI model 'Gemma 4.' Through additional training and optimization using corporate security business data, the company developed a product specialized for sensitive information detection. CTO Kim stated, "Because QEV can self-learn from each company's data and business characteristics, it is expected to be used in various environments." He added, "The significance of this achievement lies in independently developing a model with State-of-the-Art (SOTA) level performance in the DLP field by utilizing QueryPay's proprietary technology and security-specialized data for additional training and optimization based on an open-source AI model." As a result of QueryPay verifying performance using internal documents in Korean, English, and Japanese, QEV's sensitive information detection rate was 99.69%. It identified 1,277 out of 1,281 documents containing sensitive information. The detection rate of JEV API, an external commercial decision-making model, was 96.41%, which was 3.28 percentage points lower than QEV. CTO Kim revealed that QEV has also secured operational efficiency. This partnership integrates data centers, processors, and an open infrastructure platform to enhance sovereign AI capabilities. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 05:10 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google") Set ETDatacenters as your preferred source on Google ## Highlights * SK Telecom, Rebellions, and NVIDIA are collaborating on South Korea’s AI infrastructure. * Rebellions will integrate its Rebel R200 NPUs with NVIDIA’s platform via NVLink Fusion. * SK Telecom plans to deploy these integrated systems, drawing on its data center expertise. * South Korea’s government supports this initiative with significant funding for sovereign AI. South Korean telecommunications firm [SK Telecom](/tag/sk+telecom), AI chip startup [Rebellions](/tag/rebellions), and [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) have announced a collaboration to advance [South Korea](/tag/south+korea)’s [AI infrastructure](/tag/ai+infrastructure). This initiative aims to integrate [data centers](/tag/data+centers), processors, and an open infrastructure platform. Rebellions will use [NVLink Fusion](/tag/nvlink+fusion) to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to NVIDIA’s infrastructure platform. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, leveraging its data center expertise, according to a press release from NVIDIA. Jung Jai-hun, SK Telecom Chief Executive Officer and President, stated this collaboration validates the potential of next-generation [sovereign AI](/tag/sovereign+ai) infrastructure. He added it combines global AI infrastructure technology with Korean AI semiconductors. Sunghyun Park, Rebellions co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, noted that Korean technology would lead in powering AI worldwide. Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and Chief Executive Officer, highlighted Korea's talent and ambition to be a world leader in AI. The firms plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference. This will assign different stages of AI response generation to the best-suited processor architecture. The plan includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput. ### Government Support and Investment South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) supports this collaboration to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI infrastructure. Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT, said this enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA. The government will actively support this collaboration, he added, to deliver tangible results and advance cooperation with NVIDIA. Earlier this month, the South Korean government allocated KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) in its budget for 2027. This funding supports the development of physical AI, data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model. The government also plans to train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

The collaboration will see Rebellions’ next-generation R200 neural processing units ([NPUs](https://www.eenewseurope.com/en/tags/npu)) integrated into NVIDIA’s MGX rack architecture, with deployment planned at SK Telecom’s AI data centers. The agreement highlights growing opportunities for custom AI accelerators to work alongside NVIDIA GPUs in large-scale inference systems. For European semiconductor developers and data center operators, it offers a potential blueprint for combining domestic AI silicon with established computing infrastructure to support sovereign AI initiatives. ## NVLink Fusion connects custom AI silicon Rebellions plans to use NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to connect its R200 NPUs through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, targeting energy-efficient inference for frontier AI models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts architectures. The NVIDIA MGX rack architecture will provide standardized system designs, while its ecosystem of original design manufacturers and component suppliers could help Rebellions accelerate development and reduce deployment complexity. “Today’s announcement marks a turning point, opening a new chapter for sovereign AI by connecting Korea’s AI silicon and models with global systems technology,” said Sunghyun Park, cofounder and CEO of Rebellions. The companies also plan to explore disaggregated inference, splitting AI workloads between different processor architectures. Under the proposed approach, NVIDIA GPUs would handle the compute-intensive prefill stage, while Rebellions NPUs would manage token generation during decoding. This division of labor is intended to improve inference throughput and power efficiency, potentially addressing two major challenges facing AI data center operators. ## SK Telecom targets full-stack sovereign AI SK Telecom plans to deploy the systems within its AI data center infrastructure, connecting the hardware with proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, and public-facing AI services. The initiative supports Korea’s government-backed “AI for All” project and aims to strengthen domestic control over AI infrastructure, models and services. Standardizing rack footprints, power delivery and cooling through NVIDIA MGX could also simplify integration of GPU and NPU systems within existing data center environments. ## Government backing and 2028 deployment Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT is supporting the collaboration as part of a broader effort to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI capabilities and domestic semiconductor industry. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, drawing on its expertise in the data center space. “This collaboration is meaningful in that it validates the potential of next-generation sovereign AI infrastructure by combining global AI infrastructure technology with Korean AI semiconductors,” said Jung Jai-hun, SK Telecom Chief Executive Officer and President. “As a leading Korean AI silicon startup, we will lead the charge to establish Korean technology as a core pillar powering AI worldwide,” said Sunghyun Park, Rebellions co-founder and Chief Executive Officer. “Korea has the talent, technology and industrial ambition to become a world leader in AI,” said Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and Chief Executive Officer. “Sovereign AI gives nations the power to turn their language, culture and expertise into intelligence.” Together, the firms plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference. This will assign different stages of AI response generation to the processor architecture best suited to the task at hand. The plan includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput. The collaboration is supported by South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), which sees it as a means to strengthen the country’s sovereign AI infrastructure. “This collaboration with NVIDIA marks a significant step forward, as it enables Korean-developed NPUs to enter the computing infrastructure market alongside NVIDIA, a global leader in AI computing, through NVLink Fusion,” said Bae Kyung-hoon, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Science and ICT. “The government will actively support this collaboration to deliver tangible results and further advance cooperation with NVIDIA across a range of areas, including physical AI and securing GPU supply.” Earlier this month, w.media reported that the South Korean government had set aside KRW 21.3 trillion (US$ 15.83 billion) in its budget for 2027 to support the development of physical AI, data centers, and semiconductors. A further KRW 4.7 trillion (US$ 3.5 billion) has been earmarked to develop a sovereign AI model. The South Korean government will also train 2,000 specialists to lead semiconductor design and the wider chip industry. Listen to latest: The rack, not the room

In short * **NVIDIA supplies more building blocks, while partners control deployment.** NVIDIA showed agent runtimes, factory blueprints and AI data-center designs at GTC Berlin, but the highlighted demonstrations and reference designs depended on partners’ solvers, plant data, measurements or prepared sites. * **Industrial agents work inside specialist tools with restricted rights.** Cadence and Dassault Systèmes agents ran the vendors’ own engineering software, and NVIDIA’s factory agents created work orders without changing machine settings. * **AI data-center economics depend on deployment speed and output per reserved megawatt.** Factory preintegration and dynamic power allocation promise earlier and higher output, with clear trade-offs. ## The man in the foreground on the left wears glasses and has his hand near his chin in a thoughtful pose, looking at a screen showing white and colored lines on a graph. A second man is partially visible and blurred on the right, also looking at a screen.](https://247wallst.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/imageForEntry22-zbs.jpg) Jim Cramer is staying out of the AI infrastructure trade for now. On CNBC on November 10, 2026, he said: “I don’t want to make this trade because I still feel that you don’t want to be that linked to the data center yet.” He said it as the two biggest chip names in the expansion moved in opposite directions. **NVIDIA** ([NASDAQ:NVDA](https://247wallst.com/companies/NVDA/) | [NVDA Price Prediction](https://247wallst.com/companies/nvda/price-prediction)) fell 5.22% to $169.35 in Tuesday morning trading. **Broadcom** ([NASDAQ:AVGO](https://247wallst.com/companies/AVGO/)) rose 3.21% to $329.72. ## How Much of Each Company Depends on Data Centers ![](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/z29RikdXS_0/maxresdefault.jpg) What Investors Are Getting Wrong About Nvidia Being “linked to the data center” means a stock’s earnings rise or fall with how much a small group of cloud providers and AI labs spend on servers. NVIDIA is about as linked as a company can be. In the quarter it reported in August, Data Center brought in $89.02 billion of $96.22 billion in total revenue, or about 93%. Its supply obligations reached $279 billion, mostly memory bought for Vera Rubin. Days sales outstanding increased to 60 days from 45. Those are large commitments to make before you know whether demand will hold. Broadcom has more margin, and that margin is shrinking. AI semiconductors made up 56% of total revenue in fiscal Q3, up from 49% in Q2, according to the company’s [8-K earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1730168/000173016826000076/avgo-08022026x8kxex99.htm). Broadcom has six XPU customers and set up financing vehicles for two of them, Anthropic and OpenAI. Hock Tan said most AI computing demand “originates from this concentrated group who develop state-of-the-art frontier models.” He also raised a deployment risk: “Even as we ship the chips, will they be deployed on a timely basis?” ## Both Stocks Have Already Fallen NVIDIA is down 26.14% over the past month and 8.98% year to date. Part of that drop has nothing to do with data center demand. NVIDIA opened an investigation into its chief executive’s relationship with a [suspected Chinese spy](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/09/jensen-huangs-reported-ties-to-a-suspected-chinese-spy-put-trumps-purchase-of-up-to-5-million-in-nvidia-stock-back-in-the-spotlight/ "Jensen Huang's Reported Ties To A Suspected Chinese Spy Put Trump's Purchase Of Up To $5 Million In Nvidia Stock Back In The Spotlight"), and the stock fell for a second day as investors considered what it could mean (The New York Times, CNBC).
